greet.text: She is singing to a lamp, or to the space above it, and stops when your shadow falls across the threshold. The temple is cold and the lamps are not doing their job. "If you have come to look, look from the doorway. If you have come to buy, the oil is behind me, and I will not pretend the goddess needs your silver more than she needs the lamp lit."

choices.text: Do you need oil for the lamps?
choices.unavailableNote: You have no oil on you, and the temple does not take a promise of oil.

again-hymn.text: "You again." She is folding a cloth that has already been folded. "I have not found another verse, if that is what you came for. I have found three versions of the same line and none of them sing."

choices.text: It is still only a name.

again-oil.text:
The jar is gone and the lamps are still burning. She looks at you the way a woman looks at a jar that has been filled twice.

"You are becoming reliable. I am not sure it suits a traveler." She moves a stool with her foot, which is as close as she comes to asking you to stay.

choices.unavailableNote: You have no oil on you, and the temple does not take a promise of oil.

after-mystery.text:
She does not sing now. The doorway is the same and the stillness in it is not.

"You came back. Good. I have stopped singing it at strangers, and the temple has noticed." She looks at the lamp. "They have asked me to sing the palace version at the feast. The short one."

changed.text:
"Nothing changed. I only stopped."

She says it as if stopping were a kind of work. Then, because you are still there: "My sister used to say the long version was for people with time to be sad. She had time. I have a feast to prepare."

hymn.text:
"A hymn to the lady of the evening. My grandmother's version, which is longer and worse than the palace's." She sings four lines under her breath, then stops on the last one. "There is a name in it that does not belong to this city. Ninshubur."

She waits for you to say something, and when you do not, she adds, quieter: "My sister sang it at the funeral. I thought it was grief, making a word strange. It has been a year and the word is still strange."

heard.text:
"From a trader who came down from the north with a jar of bad wine and a good story. He said it the way you say a man's name, not a god's. Then he would not say it again."

She looks at the door, and then at you, and then at the door again. "My sister gave him a cup and he gave her a name. That is all I know. If you find him, do not tell him I have been singing it."

only.text: "Names are not only names. If they were, I would be out of work." She turns the lamp down, not enough to put it out. "And my sister would still be alive, which is a different argument."

oil.text: She weighs the jar in her hands, sniffs it, and pays without haggling, which means it was worth more. "Good oil," she says, as if the words cost her. "The goddess will not notice, but I will."

sources: Ninshubur in Sumerian and Akkadian sources, general
provenance.notes: Belet is invented. The theonym is attested; the trader's story, the sister and the recognition are fiction and assert no identity.

scene.goal: Hear the hymn and learn the name
scene.obstacle: Belet's grief and the temple's short version
scene.turn: She admits her sister sang it at the funeral
scene.stakes: The feast and her sister's memory
